item.title: Sensex, Nifty surge nearly 2% to post their best session since November 6
item.description: The Nifty 50 closed 1.65 per cent up at 25,791.25, and the BSE Sensex ended the day 1.88 per cent up at 83,982.08.
item.dc:creator: Shilpa Rangarajan
item.content:encoded: Benchmark indices rebounded sharply on Wednesday to their best session since November 6 — with broader markets, excluding smallcaps, also in the green — as easing commodity prices and rupee appreciation lifted over 80 per cent of index constituents and propelled Hindustan Unilever Ltd (HUL) to its biggest gain since June 2024. Across banks and fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) in the largecap space (top 250 companies), private banks gained ₹1.01 trillion and FMCG makers ₹0.82 trillion, together accounting for nearly 46 per cent of the ₹4 trillion added to the market value of NSE-listed companies, which now stands at ₹507.09 trillion. The Nifty 50 closed 1.85 per cent up at 25,819.25, and the BSE Sensex ended the day 1.82 per cent up at 83,938.28. At current levels and on a closing basis, the Nifty 50 is just 1.9 per cent away from its all-time high of 26,328.6, while the Sensex is 2.2 per cent away from its record high of 85,836.1. Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) bought a net ₹4,479.08 crore, and domestic institutional investors (DIIs) bought a net ₹4,018.72 crore, according to provisional exchange data. Brent crude fell below the $90/barrel mark intraday, and the rupee appreciated 0.7 per cent to 92.24 against the dollar.    FMCG stocks led the gains, with the Nifty FMCG index jumping 3.79 per cent to 50,143.50 as all its constituents closed in the green. The rally was driven by heavyweights HUL and ITC, with the former up 6.08 per cent and the latter rising 2.74 per cent. Nifty Consumer Durables index, meanwhile, slipped 0.13 per cent. “FMCG and pharmaceutical stocks are seeing buying interest because investors are looking for sectors that offer relatively stable earnings and lower business uncertainty amid market volatility. FMCG firms benefit from steady demand for everyday products, while pharma companies are supported by consistent healthcare demand and export opportunities,” said Somil Mehta, head of retail research at Mirae Asset Sharekhan. Of the 44 analysts tracked by Bloomberg, 33 have a “Buy” rating on HUL, nine have a “Hold”, and two have a “Sell”. The consensus target price is ₹2,194.53,  just 2.5 per cent over Wednesday’s price of ₹2,141.80. “HUL’s product portfolio primarily consists of crude oil-linked products such as detergents and soaps. Therefore, when oil corrects, it benefits companies such as HUL,” said Saurav Chaube, research analyst at Samco Securities. “Indian equities are likely to witness a gradual upward move, supported by strong foreign institutional investor (FII) buying, easing crude oil prices, a stronger rupee, and sector-specific momentum,” said Siddhartha Khemka, head of research - wealth management at Motilal Oswal.

item.title: Heavier Make in India push: ₹11,000 crore for infrastructure equipment
item.description: The scheme will provide sales-linked incentives of 8-13 per cent over five years to boost domestic manufacturing of construction and infrastructure equipment and components ...
item.dc:creator: Deepak Patel
item.content:encoded: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved a ₹11,000 crore scheme to incentivise domestic manufacturing of construction and infrastructure equipment (CIE), including tunnel boring machines (TBMs), hydraulic excavators, and ship-to-shore (STS) cranes. The scheme will provide incentives to manufacturers over five years, following a two-year gestation period for setting up manufacturing facilities. The approval comes amid concerns over India’s dependence on foreign suppliers for specialised machinery used in major infrastructure projects, particularly after China introduced export restrictions on TBMs and related equipment. The restrictions, which took effect on November 18, require exporters to obtain licences from Chinese authorities before shipping the equipment. Such machinery is critical to projects such as the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor. India will develop TBMs domestically if China restricts supplies of the critical equipment, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Tuesday, asserting that the country would not compromise its strategic interests amid Beijing’s fresh export controls. “If they don’t give us TBMs, we will develop it in India. India is not someone who will give in,” Goyal said at the Young Leaders Discourse Forum at Delhi’s Kirori Mal College. The scheme, which will be administered by the Ministry of Heavy Industries, aims to incentivise domestic manufacturing of CIE and its components and establish a dedicated testing facility in the country. It is also intended to strengthen self-reliance and position India as a key player in the global CIE market, the government said. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in a post on X, described the scheme as “a big push towards India becoming a global hub for construction and infrastructure equipment manufacturing”. Industry representatives also welcomed the initiative, with Deepak Shetty, president of the Indian Construction Equipment Manufacturers’ Association (iCEMA) and managing director and chief executive officer of JCB India, saying it was aligned with India’s infrastructure growth and manufacturing ambitions. “The Scheme for Enhancement of CIE Manufacturing Ecosystem is a timely initiative that lines up well with India’s strong infrastructure growth and manufacturing ambitions. As the construction equipment industry continues to expand, the scheme has the potential to accelerate investments in advanced technologies, promote localisation of critical components, and strengthen the domestic supplier ecosystem,” Shetty said. “By supporting the development of competitive domestic capabilities, the scheme will help position India as an increasingly important manufacturing base for construction and infrastructure equipment. It will further boost exports from India while ensuring reduction in imports, as critical electronic and hydraulic components will be manufactured in India,” he added. India’s CIE industry is currently the world’s third largest, after China and the US, with a market size of around ₹97,500 crore in 2024-25 (FY25). The government expects the market to more than double to roughly ₹2.28 trillion by 2029-30 (FY30), driven by investments in roads, ports, housing, and other infrastructure projects. The scheme will support the manufacture of technologically advanced equipment, including STS cranes, TBMs, hydraulic excavators, and off-highway trucks. It will also provide for the establishment of state-of-the-art, dedicated CIE testing facilities in the country, the government said. The scheme will run for eight years, starting 2026-27 (FY27). The first two years, FY27 and 2027-28, will be a gestation period during which companies can set up manufacturing facilities. This will be followed by five years of incentive disbursements, from 2028-29 to 2032-33 (FY33). The final year, 2033-34 (FY34), will be used to settle incentives based on incremental sales recorded in FY33. The scheme has two components. Under the first, eligible original equipment manufacturers and component manufacturers will receive sales-linked incentives ranging from 8 per cent to 13 per cent of incremental sales over five years. Incremental sales refer to the increase in sales over a prescribed base year. The second component provides a grant of up to ₹375 crore, in the form of viability gap funding (VGF), for establishing a dedicated testing facility. VGF is financial support from the government to make a project financially viable when it may not be commercially feasible on its own. The approval follows nearly two years of discussions between the construction equipment industry and the government on financial incentives to boost domestic manufacturing. In July 2024, iCEMA proposed a dedicated production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme with an outlay of ₹10,000 crore at a meeting with then finance secretary T V Somanathan, who is now the Cabinet secretary. A PLI scheme provides financial incentives to companies based on additional production or sales, encouraging them to manufacture more products domestically. In the second half of 2025, the government began inter-ministerial consultations and work on preparing a scheme for the CIE sector. The proposal was subsequently announced in the Union Budget for FY27 in February this year. Among the companies looking to develop indigenous TBMs is state-owned BEML. The company has drawn up plans to manufacture the machines in India, initially focusing on smaller models used in Metro rail, hydropower, irrigation, and water projects. BEML plans to initially develop machines with diameters ranging from 3.5 metres to 6.5 metres. Its Chairman and Managing Director Shantanu Roy told Bloomberg earlier this month that the company was onboarding a global consultant to support the development process. The company intends to develop its own technology rather than merely assemble machines using imported components. “It will be an indigenous technology...The intellectual property will be Indian,” Roy said. The case for developing domestic manufacturing capabilities has come into sharper focus following China’s export restrictions. In 2024, two TBMs manufactured by German company Herrenknecht AG at its facility in Guangzhou, China, for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project were held up at a Chinese port for more than a year. The machines eventually arrived in India in March this year. However, the latest restrictions have not yet translated into reported TBM shortages for major engineering, procurement, and construction players. Companies contacted by this newspaper said newer manufacturing facilities were helping them maintain supplies and continue project execution. In particular, Herrenknecht’s manufacturing facility in Chennai has emerged as a source of recent TBM supplies. Some companies, including the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation in its response to queries from this newspaper, cited the facility in this context. In October 2025, the German manufacturer had announced plans to set up a new plant in the southern city. TBMs are giant mechanical drills used to excavate underground passages through soil and rock. They are essential for building Metro rail corridors, railway and road tunnels, and other underground infrastructure. The new scheme could provide an added incentive for companies such as BEML to invest in domestic manufacturing. However, their eligibility for benefits will depend on the detailed guidelines and approval process under the scheme.

item.title: Cognizant in talks to take over parts of S&P Global's Capital IQ operations
item.description: Cognizant is in talks to take over data and operations staff from S&P Global's India GCC, with around 1,500 employees potentially moving to the IT services firm's payroll.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Companies / News / Cognizant in talks to take over parts of S&P Global's Capital IQ operations

Cognizant in talks to take over parts of S&P Global's Capital IQ operations Cognizant is in talks to take over data and operations staff from S&P Global's India GCC, with around 1,500 employees potentially moving to the IT services firm's payroll.

Cognizant is in discussions to take over parts of S&P Global's Capital IQ data operations in India, potentially shifting around 1,500 employees to its payroll as the financial data provider reviews the business's future. | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters 3 min read Last Updated : Nov 26 2026 | 12:13 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Cognizant is in talks to take over parts of S&P Global's Capital IQ operations in a deal that could move about 1,500 employees to the IT services provider, two people familiar with the matter said.   The proposed transfer covers employees in the data and operations team of the S&P Global unit's India global capability centre (GCC), who would move to Cognizant's payroll under the arrangement, the people said, speaking on condition of anonymity.   The discussions are ongoing and the terms could change or the talks could fall apart, the people said.   The negotiations come as S&P Global reviews the future of Capital IQ and associated data businesses.

S&P said on October 27 it was exploring strategic alternatives, including a potential separation, for Capital IQ and associated data businesses, which constitute the majority of its Kensho Data & Platforms unit within Market Intelligence. Also Read

LG Electronics India promoter may offload 2% stake for ₹2,320.5 crore

JioStar starts fresh layoffs as television business faces mounting pressure

PTC Industries bags major defence order for 400 tonnes of titanium

Dalmia Bharat approves ₹700 crore share buyback via open market route

Bisleri challenges FSSAI's unsafe-sample finding, says water safe to drink

Cognizant has a longstanding relationship with S&P Global and previously performed the services now under discussion before the financial-data provider brought them in-house, one of the people said.   S&P Global declined to comment on the potential transaction, saying it does not comment on speculation concerning its "contingent labour partners". Cognizant did not respond to emailed requests for comment.   Businesses can use such deals to cut costs and focus on core operations, with AI adding pressure to seek productivity gains and rethink technology and data work, industry experts said.

"Moving the India data operations to Cognizant first makes the asset lighter and more sellable and suits the AI/LLM-ready data direction. It is a typical pre-divestiture play," said Phil Fersht, founder of market research firm HFS Research.   Gaurav Vasu, founder of market research firm UnearthInsight, said companies typically carve out operations when growth or profitability is under pressure, or when management concludes outsourcing would allow them to focus more on their core business.   "They will usually bring in an IT vendor for one specific service or business unit," Vasu said.   UnearthInsight estimates the annual "loaded" cost of an employee at an S&P-like global capability centre, including expenses beyond salary, at about $25,000 to $30,000.

On that basis, the cost associated with 1,500 employees would be roughly $38 million to $45 million a year, Vasu said, and would typically be factored into a multi-year services contract.   Similar transfers have emerged elsewhere.   In October, Best Buy agreed to transition its India GCC to Tata Consultancy Services under a multi-year agreement, with the retailer's India employees moving to TCS.   Those deals run alongside a much bigger expansion of global companies' in-house operations in India.   India's GCC industry generated $98.4 billion in fiscal 2026, nearly reaching IT industry body Nasscom and consultancy Zinnov's 2030 forecast four years early. The industry's 2,117 centres employed about 2.36 million people.

item.title: New US tariff may give India edge over Asian peers if trade deal done: GTRI
item.description: GTRI said a proposed 17% US tariff under a trade pact would give India a slight edge over Asian competitors, while the rate could rise to 25% without an agreement.
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / New US tariff may give India edge over Asian peers if trade deal done: GTRI

New US tariff may give India edge over Asian peers if trade deal done: GTRI GTRI said a proposed 17% US tariff under a trade pact would give India a slight edge over Asian competitors, while the rate could rise to 25% without an agreement.

India's proposed tariff rate under a potential US trade pact could be lower than those faced by several Asian competitors, giving Indian exporters a slight advantage, according to GTRI. | Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 26 2026 | 12:11 AM IST

Listen to This Article

India could face a 17 per cent US tariff if a bilateral trade agreement is finalised, giving it a slight edge over several Asian competitors, but the rate could rise to 25 per cent without a pact, think tank GTRI said on Wednesday, warning of possible additional duties or import quotas.   India must reject the trade deal and instead answer allegations sector by sector, it said.   The answers should clearly show that India's investment serves domestic buyers, overseas customers, and future demand, the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI) said.   "Under the proposed USTR tariffs, Indian imports face a 17 per cent tariff if a trade pact is finalised, offering a calculated 1 per cent edge over Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand (18 per cent deal rate) and a 3 per cent edge over Vietnam and China (20 per cent deal rate), while rising up to 25 per cent without a deal, alongside the risk that an adverse USTR ruling could bring further duties or import quotas," GTRI Founder Ajay Srivastava said.

These new tariffs proposed on November 25 by the US Trade Representative (USTR) were under Section 301 excess-capacity investigations. Also Read

Section 301 probe: India rejects US claim of structural excess capacity

US proposes up to 25% tariff on India, offers 17% upon trade deal

Trump rebuilds global tariff wall, India faces proposed duties of up to 25%

US proposes new tariffs on 14 trading partners, including India and China

Asian stocks tumble as AI rebound stumbles, US tariff threats loom

Initiated by the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) on March 11, 2026, against 16 economies, the proposed duties target 14 trading partners while excluding Mexico and Norway for now.   "By deploying a dual-rate structure, threatening steep baseline tariffs against countries that refuse a pact while offering lower rates to those that sign, Washington reclaims the bargaining power to impose duties at will and extract unilateral concessions, allowing a government to secure tariff relief even if the industrial capacity that prompted the investigation remains unchanged," he said.

For India, the Section 301 investigation flags potential excess capacity or export surpluses across seven sectors: solar modules (where capacity is nearly triple domestic demand), petrochemicals, steel, textiles, health-related goods, construction materials, and automotive products.   More From This Section
